question: My small business has a dispute over the award of a low-value federal contract. What federal office should I check for a complaint process?
generated_answer: You may contact the Small Business Office at the federal agency that awarded the contract. If the federal agency does not have a Small Business Office, you may contact the Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization, U.S. Department of Defense, 1400 Defense Pentagon, Washington, DC 20301-1400, or call 703-682-7274. Do I have to use a certain format when submitting a protest to the Government Accountability Office? No. The Government Accountability Office (GAO) will consider any written statement it receives that alleges a contract was improperly awarded. You should clearly identify yourself as the party filing the protest. In addition, you should include the solicitation or contract number, the name and address of your firm, and a list of witnesses with their addresses. You should also include any supporting documentation in your protest. How do I find out which federal agencies are required to establish and carry out small business programs? The Small Business Act requires that all Federal Agencies receiving more than $500,000 in appropriations establish a Director-level Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization (OSDBU). Agencies with less than $500,000 in appropriations are required to establish and carry out small business programs within the Agency's various components. For more information on the Small Business Act and the requirements of Federal Agencies, please visit our About Us page.
